text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working out the payoff formula for this public goods game, where each token kept in one's own account earns 1 point but costs every other member 0.3 points, while contributions to the group account presumably return some shared benefit I need to define.

Comparing the two options, keeping tokens gives the individual 1 point versus only 0.3 from the group account per token, making "keep everything" the dominant strategy regardless of what others do—even though contributing is better for total social welfare since the externality from keeping is so costly to the group. I'm now calculating what the Nash equilibrium payoff looks like when everyone keeps all 20 tokens.

The externality from others' tokens is beyond my control, so repetition across 10 rounds doesn't change the dominance of this strategy since there's no mechanism to punish defection that affects my own payoff. I'll settle on contributing 0 to the group account as the rational answer, with a brief explanation of the reasoning.

So this is a classic social dilemma—selfishly I should keep everything private since my own payoff is highest that way, but if everyone defects, mutual losses from others' private-keeping would drag down my total earnings far more than if everyone had cooperated. I need to decide whether to prioritize my own payoff maximization or push toward the mutually beneficial cooperative outcome.
